title: Aster and the Moon-Cake Treat
markdown:
Way up high in the world, where the wind likes to whisper secrets through the pine trees and the stars sometimes twinkle so low they tickle your nose, there lived a kind young elf named Aster. He made his home in the Northwind Heights, a truly lovely place with trees that chimed like little bells when the breeze danced through them, and mountains that wore fuzzy white cloud hats. Not too long ago Aster had received a most delightful gift: a tiny kitten, as soft and white as the freshest fallen snow. This kitten’s paws were so bouncy, and her eyes shone with a happy sparkle, so Aster named her Sparkle. She was his dearest companion, always ready for an adventure.

One evening, just as the sky was turning all sorts of beautiful colours, like a painter had spilled his pinks and oranges and purples, Aster’s mother gave him something very special. It was a moon-cake, round and plump, and it smelled like the sweetest honey mixed with the sparkle of faraway stars. “Aster, my little ray of sunshine,” his mother said, her voice as soft as the down on a baby bird’s wing, “this is for your Grandmother Elara. She lives just on the other side of the Whispering Falls. Now, be a swift little bird. The moon will be climbing up, up, up very soon, and this cake is happiest when it is still bathed in its gentle glow.”

So Aster carefully placed Sparkle into his soft pouch, just letting her tiny nose and bright eyes peek out. Together they set off into the whispering pine woods. The trees tinkled a merry tune as Aster padded along, and the air was filled with the lovely fresh scent of pine needles. Sparkle wriggled with pure delight, her little tail wagging like a happy flag. “Are we going to see Grandma, Sparkle?” Sparkle let out a tiny happy meow, which Aster understood perfectly as yes, yes, we are.

The forest floor felt like a soft green carpet under Aster’s feet, all made of bouncy moss, and little bluebell flowers peeked out like tiny lamps, guiding their way. Aster’s eyes were on the sky, watching the big friendly moon begin its slow steady journey upwards. He could almost feel the warmth of Grandmother Elara’s cozy cottage, waiting for them beside the gentle sound of the Whispering Falls.

All this walking, breathing in the fresh piney air, and feeling the happy excitement of the journey made Aster’s tummy start to do a little rumble-tumble. It was a very small rumble, mind you, but it was there. He could not help but peek inside the paper that held the moon-cake. It was still so beautiful, so perfectly round, and it seemed to have a soft friendly glow all its own. Just one tiny little nibble would not hurt, would it? Grandma will have plenty, and she loves sharing. He reached out his finger, just the very tip, to touch the delicious-smelling edge, when suddenly he heard a little rustling sound coming from behind a big mossy rock nearby.

A tiny rustle, like dry leaves whispering. Aster’s ears pricked up, and the fresh scent of pine needles seemed to sharpen in the air as a cheerful dusting of flour, still, warm from the oven, drifted nearby. Out shuffled a goblin. But this was not any scary goblin you might imagine. This goblin was round and rosy-cheeked, with a very tall baker’s hat tilted a little sideways on his head, and a cheerful dusting of flour right on the tip of his nose. He was carrying a basket that seemed to be overflowing with the most wonderfully smelling pastries Aster had ever seen. Aster blinked, his eyes wide. “Well, hello there, little elf. Are you perhaps a little bit lost? Or maybe you are just admiring my rather scrumptious buns?”

Aster held the moon-cake just a little bit closer, feeling a tiny bit shy. “Oh, no, sir. I am on my way to my Grandmother Elara’s cottage, and I was… well, I was just feeling a little bit hungry, to be honest.”

The goblin baker let out a chuckle, a sound that reminded Aster of warm dough puffing up softly in the oven. “Oh, a nibble, is it? Ah, yes, that is the curious thing about moon-cakes, you know, they do have a way of tempting one. But why just nibble when you can have a whole, delicious treat?” He began to rummage gently through his overflowing basket, and with a flourish he pulled out a pastry that was shaped like a tiny golden star. It smelled like warm cinnamon and pure sunshine. “Here you are, young elf. Have this one. It is a Star-Puff. I just made them fresh this very morning.”

As Aster took the Star-Puff, his eyes grew even wider. It was delightfully warm in his hands, and the sweetness of its scent filled the air. He took a tiny bite. It tasted like warm sunshine and happy thoughts. He stood there for a moment, just enjoying the lovely warmth of the Star-Puff, the soft whisper of the pines, and the gentle rustle of leaves around him. Then, as he looked past the goblin’s friendly face, Aster saw something truly extraordinary peeking out from behind the goblin’s basket. Two little eyes, as shiny and round as smooth pebbles, and a tiny snout that looked like a delicate velvety mushroom. It was a little dragon hatchling. It looked so very small and perhaps a tiny bit shy, but its little tail gave a happy wiggle when it smelled the warm sweet Star-Puff.

“A little dragon.”

“Indeed.” The goblin patted his basket with a floury hand. “His name is Flicker. He just loves the smell of baking, so he hitched a ride with me for a little stroll. Don’t you worry, he is not one bit scary. He just enjoys sweet things and a nice warm hug or two.” Flicker, as if to agree, let out a tiny puff of smoke that smelled faintly of perfectly toasted marshmallows.

Aster smiled a big happy smile. His tummy was now wonderfully content, and he had made two new delightful friends. He did not even feel like nibbling the moon-cake anymore. “Thank you very much. This Star-Puff is absolutely perfect.”

With a friendly wave to the goblin baker and a little nod to Flicker, Aster and Sparkle continued their journey. Flicker the dragon hatchling watched them go, giving another tiny happy squeak. The moon was higher in the sky now, and its silvery light cast a soft peaceful glow over the whole world. Soon Aster heard the gentle soothing sound of the Whispering Falls. And there, just as he had imagined, was Grandmother Elara’s cozy cottage, with a warm inviting light shining brightly from the window.

He gently pushed open the door, and there was Grandmother Elara, her eyes twinkling just like the stars, ready with the biggest warmest hug. “Aster, my dear child. And Sparkle too. And what is this wonderful sweet scent that fills my cottage?”

Aster proudly presented the beautiful moon-cake, still holding its soft moonlight glow. “And I brought you this, Grandma.” He held out the delicious Star-Puff for her to share. Sparkle hopped out of Aster’s pouch, purring and rubbing her soft fur against Grandmother Elara’s legs. The gentle moonlight poured in through the window, filling the cozy cottage with a feeling of perfect peace and safety. The pines chimed like little bells. The cake kept its glow. Nobody had taken a nibble after all.
characters: Aster (young elf who carries a moon-cake), Sparkle (a white kitten with bouncy paws)
author: StoryGen Community
